summary.title: status --selector should not open index.sqlite
summary.what: sync now writes index.meta.json beside the body SQLite index after the write connection commits and closes. The sidecar holds per-source coverage records, session/message counts, and the source-file meta cache, plus a sqlite+wal identity. status and find coverage proofs read that sidecar when the identity still matches and open index.sqlite only when the sidecar is missing, corrupt, or stale. Freshness fingerprints stay byte-identical to the sync-time scan.
summary.why: After Bet 1/2, warm status --selector still opened the 375MB body database just to load coverage rows, counts, and file-meta cache. That open was the remaining cost above the Node process floor. Coverage proof does not need message bodies or FTS. Extends int_96a8fc73 (one proof, one open) and int_d189e8a1 (sync-only file-meta cache) by moving the metadata plane out of the body file.

decisions.chose: A JSON sidecar next to the DB (index.sqlite -> index.meta.json) written only by sync after the SQLite commit.
decisions.rationale: Status then does a small JSON read plus sqlite+wal stat. No second SQLite file, no daemon, and no new freshness cache layer on top of source_file_meta_cache.
rejected: A tiny second SQLite for metadata
Trusting stored fingerprints without a live covering snapshot
Having status write the sidecar on fallback

decisions.point: How dual-write stays safe if sync crashes between commit and sidecar
decisions.chose: Snapshot sidecar payload from the open write connection, checkpoint WAL best-effort, close, then atomically write the sidecar with the post-close sqlite+wal identity. Readers treat identity mismatch as stale and fall back to SQLite.
decisions.rationale: Sidecar is never newer than the committed body index. A crash after commit leaves the old sidecar, which fails the identity check, so the next status opens SQLite and sees the committed coverage.
rejected: Writing the sidecar before the SQLite transaction commits
Using only sqlite mtime/size and ignoring WAL
Failing the whole sync when sidecar write fails

decisions.point: What happens when the sidecar is absent
decisions.chose: Read-only SQLite fallback, same proof semantics as 0.4.1. Tests that only replaceCoverage still open the DB once.
decisions.rationale: Existing indexes and unit tests keep working until the next sync. Sync remains the only writer.
rejected: Requiring a sidecar before status can run
Letting status persist a sidecar on fallback

rejected.alternative: A watcher/daemon that keeps coverage hot
rejected.reason: Violates the product boundary that Sherlog stays a CLI with manual incremental sync.

rejected.alternative: Another persistent freshness cache besides the sync-time file-meta projection
rejected.reason: int_96a8fc73 and int_d189e8a1 already rejected stacking caches. The sidecar is a projection of the same sync-time rows, not a new freshness rule.

review_notes: npm run check: tsc --noEmit && vitest 252/252. PR #103 CI test job passed in 49s and merged as 4ed84d0.

Live Codex index: persistIndexSidecarAfterWrite wrote a 277KB sidecar beside the 375MB DB in 113ms. Checkout status --source codex --selector {"kind":"all"} --json is dbOpens=0, ~60ms warm vs ~40ms node dist/cli.js --version floor. Installed 0.4.1 still opens SQLite (warm dbMs ~10ms, cold first open dbMs ~107ms).
No JSON contract change. Global shlog remains 0.4.1 until the 0.4.2 registry release. After upgrade, the next sync writes the sidecar; until then status falls back to SQLite.

architectural_claims: Coverage/index metadata for status and find proofs is a sync-written sidecar projection, not a reason to open the body SQLite index.
Sidecar validity is the post-close sqlite+wal identity; mismatch or absence falls back to one read-only SQLite open.
sync remains the only Sherlog state writer; status/find never persist the sidecar.
behavioral_changes: After a successful sync, status --selector and find coverage probes set dbOpens=0 when the sidecar identity matches.
Missing, corrupt, or identity-stale sidecar falls back to the previous one-open SQLite path.
Direct replaceCoverage without sync still opens SQLite once.

data_model_changes.name: index.meta.json
data_model_changes.migration_notes: Created on the next successful sync beside index.sqlite. Until then, status/find open SQLite as in 0.4.1.

migration_notes: No database schema change. First sync after upgrade writes the sidecar. Pre-0.4.2 CLIs ignore the file. Do not treat the sidecar as a retrieval source of truth.
